subject.title: David with the Head of Goliath
subject.creator: Caravaggio

lead.credit: David with the Head of Goliath-Caravaggio (1610) — Wikimedia Commons

sentences.text: Why does a boy who just killed a giant look like he lost?
This is David with the Head of Goliath, painted by Caravaggio.
Everyone knows the story of the shepherd boy who beat the giant.
In the faith of the time, it stood for good beating evil.
And the picture seems to agree.
He holds the sword and lifts the head by its hair.
But look at the severed face.
Caravaggio painted his own face on it.
According to his biographer Bellori, Cardinal Scipione Borghese commissioned the painting in 1606.
That cardinal had the power to pardon Caravaggio for murder.
And David looks down with sadness and compassion.
It's a killer asking for mercy.
So is this a giant's defeat, or the painter offering up his own head?

meta.title: He Painted His Own Severed HEAD... and Sent It to the Judge #history #art
meta.description: David with the Head of Goliath by Caravaggio hangs in the Galleria Borghese in Rome. Caravaggio painted himself as Goliath; if the painting was a gift to Cardinal Scipione Borghese, who could pardon him for murder, it can be read as a plea for mercy.
meta.question: A giant's defeat, or the painter's own head?

sources.claim: David with the Head of Goliath is a painting by the Italian Baroque master Caravaggio.

The biographical interest of the painting adds another layer of meaning to an already complex work, David and Goliath standing for Christ and Satan and the triumph of good over evil in orthodox Christ
This bond is further complicated by the fact that Caravaggio has depicted himself as Goliath, while the model for David is il suo Caravaggino ("his own little Caravaggio").
